central_question: Conjecture 3.12 states: for every fixed k, the class of tournaments of twin-width <= k is chiVec-bounded ('chi-arrow-bounded'): there exists a binding function f such that chiVec(T) <= f(omegaVec(T)) for every tournament T with tww(T) <= k. Here chiVec is the dichromatic number, omegaVec(T) = min over vertex orderings of the clique number of the back-edge graph, and tww is twin-width. This is an ASYMPTOTIC existence-of-binding-function claim, so it cannot be PROVED by finite enumeration. The seeded lean is DISPROVE: a counterexample is a concrete finite FAMILY with bounded tww, bounded omegaVec, and growing chiVec. The exact handle: S_k = Delta(1, S_{k-1}, S_{k-1}) has chiVec(S_k)=k and (k>=2) tww=1, so the binding-function behaviour at twin-width 1 is governed ENTIRELY by how omegaVec(S_k) grows; the paper states omegaVec(S_k) is KNOWN only for k<=4 (=1,2,2,3) and is OPEN for k>=5. If omegaVec(S_k) stayed bounded while chiVec=k grows, the S_k family at tww=1 would REFUTE the conjecture. The primary measurement target is therefore omegaVec(S_k) for k>=5.
